final_candidates.decision_summary: Lys119 forms the catalytic PLP Schiff base in CBS; mutating it to alanine eliminates cofactor binding and completely abolishes enzymatic activity.
Introduces a charge reversal at the PLP-binding Lys119 residue, severely disrupting active-site electrostatics and preventing Schiff base formation.
Cys52 is an essential axial heme ligand; alanine substitution disrupts iron coordination and severely compromises CBS enzymatic activity.

stop_reason.detail: Top-3 high-confidence loss-of-function mutations targeting critical catalytic and cofactor-binding residues have been identified and validated against sequence coordinates.

history.rationale: Lys119 forms the catalytic Schiff base with the PLP cofactor; mutation to Ala prevents PLP binding and abolishes enzyme activity.
Lys119 forms the essential internal Schiff base with PLP; alanine substitution abolishes cofactor binding and catalytic activity completely.
Cys52 acts as an essential axial ligand coordinating heme; substitution to Ala disrupts heme binding and causes loss of function.
Cys52 serves as an essential axial heme ligand; mutating it to alanine disrupts heme coordination and severely impairs enzyme function.
His65 serves as the histidine axial ligand to heme; mutating it to Ala compromises cofactor coordination and abolishes catalytic activity.
His65 is the second axial ligand for heme binding; alanine substitution prevents heme integration and abolishes enzymatic activity.
Replacing the active-site Schiff base lysine with glutamic acid introduces a charge reversal, completely preventing PLP attachment and activity.
Charge inversion at the active site Lys119 disrupts PLP binding and pocket electrostatics, ensuring total loss of function.
Ser147 lies within the conserved PLP phosphate-binding loop; mutating to Ala removes hydrogen bonding to PLP phosphate, disabling activity.
Ser147 interacts with the phosphate group of PLP; mutating it weakens PLP binding and diminishes CBS activity.
Thr150 is located in the PLP-anchoring motif; substitution to Ala severely impairs cofactor binding and enzymatic turnover.
Thr150 contributes key hydrogen bonds to the PLP phosphate moiety, essential for proper cofactor orientation.
Asp120 is adjacent to the catalytic Lys119 and stabilizes active site architecture; substitution to Ala reduces activity.
Asp120 stabilizes the protonated pyridinium ring of PLP; removing its carboxylate impairs catalysis.
Gly305 is part of a conserved flexible loop near the active cleft; introducing a bulky charged glutamate disrupts structure and function.
Gly305 is located in a conserved loop near the catalytic core; introducing a bulky charged glutamate causes severe steric clash.
Gly307 is located in the central core region; substitution with glutamate creates major steric clashes that abolish CBS activity.
Gly307 lies within the active site loop where glutamic acid substitution perturbs local backbone conformation and catalytic entry.
